notes: I think I was close to getting a submission ready, but I kept coming up with unhandled edge cases. Time got the better of me, had to quit.
aiExplanation: This solution finds the longest run of **consecutive integers** you can build when each number is allowed to stay as-is or be increased by exactly one. It first **sorts** `nums` so smaller values are processed before larger ones, then uses a `Map` called `dp` where `dp.get(v)` stores the length of the longest consecutive sequence that ends with the value `v`. For each number `x`, it considers two choices: bumping it to `x + 1`, which extends whatever sequence ended at `x` (so `dp.set(x + 1, ...)` takes the max of its current value and `dp.get(x) + 1`), or keeping it as `x`, which extends the sequence that ended at `x - 1` (so `dp.set(x, ...)` takes the max of its current value and `dp.get(x - 1) + 1`). The `?? 0` fallbacks handle values that have not been seen yet, and the `x + 1` update is done first so that the "keep" option does not accidentally feed into the "increase" option for the same element. After each step, `ans` is updated with the best length ending at either `x` or `x + 1`, and the final `ans` is returned as the maximum number of selectable elements.
